olivia: Blocking on docs PR #638 — I added guidance for retrying on 429/503 and an example using an Idempotency-Key header. CI preview passed but runtime folks: need confirmation on server dedupe semantics and SDK default retry behavior before merging.
sam: can you paste the snippet and the prose you added? important to be precise here.
olivia: snippet in PR:

HTTP example:
POST /v1/generate
Headers: {
  "Content-Type": "application/json",
  "Idempotency-Key": "abc-123"
}
Body: {"model":"x-large","input":"Hello"}

PR text currently: "Set an Idempotency-Key to avoid duplicate charges when retrying on 429/503. The server will deduplicate requests with the same key." Is that too strong?
devops: hold merge until runtime confirms semantics. There are nuances: dedupe window, what counts as the same request (body equality, route, model version), and streaming/function-call interactions.
sam: runtime clarifications:
- Server deduplicates non-streaming, non-function-calling requests when an Idempotency-Key is present and the payload (request method + route + body bytes) is identical.
- Deduplication window: 10 minutes by default (configurable per-deployment). If a matching request arrives after the window, it's treated as a new request.
- If the original request completed (200), retries with same key return the original response (cached), subject to retention TTL.
- If the original request failed or is still in progress, retries will either return the failure or attach to in-flight work when possible.
- Streaming requests, function-calling requests that have side effects (tool calls, webhooks), and requests that invoke external actions are NOT automatically deduplicated; SDKs should not retry them automatically without explicit opt-in.
- Deduplication requires exact body equality; small differences (ordering of JSON keys, whitespace in raw body for bytes comparison) may prevent a match. We canonicalize JSON before comparison for HTTP APIs, but SDKs must ensure deterministic serialization.

olivia: good detail. Can you suggest an updated one-line replacement for the docs so we don't overpromise?
sam: suggested sentence: "When present, Idempotency-Key enables server-side deduplication for standard non-streaming requests with identical request payloads; the router retains dedupe state for a limited window (default 10 minutes). Streaming or side-effecting requests are exempt from automatic deduplication."
devops: also add a short bullet list of practical guidance: 1) Use Idempotency-Key for non-streaming generate/embeddings calls you plan to retry. 2) Avoid automatic SDK retries for streaming or function-calling requests — surface a manual retry helper. 3) Ensure SDK serializes payload deterministically so the server can match keys.
olivia: SDK default behavior note: our JS/Python SDKs currently retry on network errors and 429 with exponential backoff up to 3 attempts for idempotent-suspected endpoints. But I need confirmation: does the SDK set Idempotency-Key automatically on retry?
sam: SDKs should not set Idempotency-Key automatically for customers unless the call is known idempotent. Current policy: SDK will auto-generate an Idempotency-Key for retries on POST generate/embeddings only when the request has no streaming or function call flags and when the user has not provided their own key. We should document that.
noliivia: (typo) — Olivia: OK, please add that exact sentence. Also we must call out logs: server logs use snake_case field names and will show dedupe hits for diagnosis.
devops: one more edge: customers using proxies that normalize headers might strip Idempotency-Key; mention that in migration notes.
ci-bot: preview for PR #638 deployed: https://preview.docs.redwood.ai/pr/638 (status: success) :white_check_mark:
olivia: thanks — I'll update PR prose with sam's suggested sentence, add the practical guidance bullets, and a short code example showing SDK-provided idempotency behavior and how to opt-out by setting your own key.

sam: quick additional note: retention TTL for cached successful responses is configurable per-account; mention that "cached responses are subject to an account-level TTL" in parentheses.
olivia: will add parenthetical about TTL and the proxy header warning. Pushing now. PTAL when CI updates.
devops: LGTM after the tiny TTL note. Please ensure the SDK example clarifies automatic generation only for non-streaming calls.
olivia: pushed update. PTAL.
